Since Bun 1.4.4, an `error` event that nothing listens for is an uncaught exception, as with `ws` in Node.js. A refused connection ends the process.

The rule only runs in files that import or require `ws` or `ws/…`. It follows an `import()` only if it's awaited.

A socket that's returned, stored in an object or passed to a function isn't reported, because it can get its listener there.

`bun lint --upgrade` runs this rule. See [Upgrade Bun](/lint#upgrade-bun).

{/* Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit this section. */}

## Configure

Off by default. To turn it on:

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"bun/ws-require-error-listener" = "error" # or "warn"
```

{/* End of the generated section. */}

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad {"count": 2} */}
```ts
import WebSocket, { WebSocketServer } from "ws";

const client = new WebSocket(url);
client.on("message", print);

new WebSocketServer({ port }).on("connection", socket => {
  socket.on("message", print);
});
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```ts
import WebSocket, { WebSocketServer } from "ws";

const client = new WebSocket(url);
client.on("message", print);
client.on("error", console.error);

new WebSocketServer({ port }).on("connection", socket => {
  socket.on("message", print);
  socket.on("error", console.error);
});
```
